summary: Configured node1 with a persistent firewalld policy: SSH is allowed from any address, TCP/9000 is accepted only from node2 (10.100.94.11/32), and rejected from node3 and all other IPv4 sources. All three nodes were restarted sequentially and recovered with changed boot identities.
actions_performed: Kept SSH enabled in node1's public zone.
Added a priority -100 accept rule for node2 to TCP/9000.
Added a priority 100 catch-all reject rule for TCP/9000.
Verified live access from node2 and rejection from node3.
Restarted node1, node2, and node3 one at a time and verified recovery.

evidence.summary: firewalld is active and enabled. Runtime and permanent rules accept 10.100.94.11/32 on TCP/9000 before rejecting all other IPv4 sources; SSH remains allowed.

evidence.requirement: Live source-scoped access after all restarts
evidence.summary: With node1 listening on its managed IP, node2 received final-policy-ok on TCP/9000, node3 received connect error 111, and both received the OpenSSH banner on TCP/22.
Baseline boot ID d546da19-398f-473c-b85c-afdd17037523 changed to 2a83329b-8b1e-4cd5-adbd-6d28bc4ab049. firewalld, sshd, SSH permission, and both runtime and permanent rich rules recovered.
Baseline boot ID 49dafad6-5cc2-457a-b0f6-1219740a651e changed to 46d990a8-548f-4b38-ba9e-60a91df3aa67. sshd and node1 connectivity recovered, including node2's permitted TCP/9000 access.
Baseline boot ID 54089086-53d1-408b-a22f-57b1dea70e03 changed to 9196db3b-2783-405b-916e-3886fc5a4808. sshd and node1 SSH connectivity recovered while TCP/9000 remained rejected.
